content: 1. The concurrent use of etrasimod with antineoplastic, immune-modulating, or non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapies has not been studied. This combination may increase the risk of additive immunosuppressive effects, leading to a heightened risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided during and in the weeks following etrasimod administration. 2. Etrasimod and tivozanib may mutually enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 3. A transient decrease in heart rate and AV conduction delays may occur when initiating etrasimod. While stable beta-blocker treatment with etrasimod did not show additive effects on heart rate reduction, the risk of additive heart rate reduction when initiating beta-blocker therapy with stable etrasimod treatment or with other heart rate-reducing drugs is unknown. 35. A transient decrease in heart rate and AV conduction delays may occur when initiating etrasimod. Etrasimod may increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes when co-administered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging drugs. 36.
